assumptions_made: The Hugging Face dataset was not suitable for this experiment's specific requirements, so synthetic data was generated instead
The synthetic data uses a reasonable range of trait values and correlations to simulate realistic group structures
The experiment assumes a fixed within-group variance of 1.0 for simplicity
The experiment uses 10 groups with 20 observations each to balance computational feasibility with statistical power
The experiment runs 1000 replicates per heterogeneity level to ensure stable estimates
The true population mean is assumed to be 0 for calculating bias
Confidence intervals are calculated using standard normal distribution with z-score of 1.96
The shrinkage estimator uses a simple variance-ratio approach for demonstration purposes

results.hypothesis: Test whether a hierarchical estimator has lower variance than a pooled estimator under group heterogeneity.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: The pooled estimator at the same heterogeneity level.
results.success_criteria: The shrinkage estimator has lower variance at every heterogeneity level without coverage dropping below 0.90.
results.notes: The shrinkage estimator's coverage drops below 0.90 at some heterogeneity levels.
results.methodological_validity: mixed real and synthetic inputs — findings are NOT interpretable as evidence; the synthetic inputs are listed in data_provenance.json
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.
